usageNotes: Use this to modify an existing firewall rule on an LXC container by its zero-based position index; requires VM.Config.Network on the container. Supply `digest` (from the GET rules response) to guard against concurrent edits overwriting each other. To reorder a rule without changing its properties, set only `moveto`; all other body fields are ignored when `moveto` is present.

examples.summary: Change an existing inbound TCP rule at position 2 to DROP port 23 (Telnet) and add a comment

tips: Position (pos) is zero-based; use GET /nodes/{node}/lxc/{vmid}/firewall/rules to list current rules and their positions before editing.
Setting `moveto` to a new index repositions the rule atomically; combine with a separate PUT call if you also need to change rule properties.
Use the `delete` param (comma-separated field names) to unset optional fields like `source`, `dest`, or `comment` rather than sending an empty string.
The container firewall must be enabled at both the container level and the host/cluster level for rules to take effect.
LXC interface names in `iface` must follow the net\d+ pattern (e.g., net0), not arbitrary names as allowed for host rules.
